articles.title: Scoring all seven: a personality quiz that refuses to hand you just one label
articles.excerpt: Most personality quizzes are built to give you a sticker. You answer some questions, the page dramatic-reveals "You are the Visionary!", and that's the whole product. I kept wondering what would happe…
articles.body: Most personality quizzes are built to give you a sticker. You answer some questions, the page dramatic-reveals "You are the Visionary!", and that's the whole product. I kept wondering what would happen if a quiz refused to pick a winner — so I built one around the seven deadly sins, and it shows you all seven scores every time. Here's the thinking behind it, plus the history rabbit hole that made the theme fit. The theme is older than any modern personality framework The seven deadly sins are, in effect, the medieval West's trait model. The interesting part is how messy the path was: the 4th-century monk Evagrius Ponticus started with eight "thoughts", Gregory the Great later merged two and added one, and the modern seven only settled after centuries of edits.

articles.body: Two AI Agents Made the Right Decision. Together, They Corrupted the Same State. The hidden concurrency problem behind multi-agent AI systems Something is interesting about debugging intelligent systems: sometimes, every component appears to be doing exactly what it was designed to do, and the overall system still produces the wrong result. I have been thinking about this increasingly as AI agents move beyond answering questions and start performing tasks across business applications, databases, APIs and enterprise workflows. We have spent considerable time discussing whether an AI agent can reason correctly, whether it can remember previous interactions, whether it can reject outdated information and whether it can follow instructions.

articles.title: Running bd commands in parallel was slower than running them in turn
articles.excerpt: bd board is a local dashboard for bd (beads), the issue tracker that keeps its data in your repo. It has no database of its own: every screen is built by shelling out to the bd CLI, and one page can n…
articles.body: bd board is a local dashboard for bd (beads) , the issue tracker that keeps its data in your repo. It has no database of its own: every screen is built by shelling out to the bd CLI, and one page can need several calls for the beads, the statuses, the epics and the knowledge entries. Those calls do not depend on each other, so the first version ran them at the same time. Running them one after another turned out to be faster. Why parallel is slower bd uses an embedded Dolt database, and Dolt locks it while a process works. Concurrent calls on the same project end up waiting for each other, and together they take longer than the same calls run in turn.

articles.excerpt: Every month it's the same routine for anyone who invoices or reconciles: statements arrive as PDFs, and the numbers need to be in a spreadsheet before you can sort, filter, or pivot them. Copy-pasting…
articles.body: Every month it's the same routine for anyone who invoices or reconciles: statements arrive as PDFs, and the numbers need to be in a spreadsheet before you can sort, filter, or pivot them. Copy-pasting out of a PDF viewer mangles the columns, and retyping a few hundred rows by hand is where errors creep in. I've been running BankStatementSheets as part of a monthly close checklist: drop each statement file in get an Excel or CSV back with one row per transaction dates land as real dates, amounts stay numeric, balances get their own column paste into a master sheet and let pivot tables finish the job Nothing fancy — it just removes the most error-prone step of the monthly tidy-up.

articles.body: The application executes the tool requests a model returns. If the model keeps asking for another lookup, your loop decides whether to keep spending time and memory or stop with the evidence already collected. Ollama’s chat API can return several tool calls in one response. Count both rounds and individual calls, limit each tool result, and reject missing or unknown tool names. The loop below also gives Ollama fetches a shared deadline; tools need cancellation or execution limits appropriate to their own work. A bounded local example Prerequisites: Node.js 20 or newer, Ollama running on localhost, and a model that supports tool calling already available in Ollama. articles.title: 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA’s SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket?
articles.excerpt: NASA's SkyFall helicopters are set to be transported to Mars on the agency's first nuclear rocket, but some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one.
articles.body: The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket. NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet . But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one.

articles.title: The Lego Star Trek bridge diorama set should be your gateway to finally watching the Original Series
articles.excerpt: Dammit Jim, I'm a doctor, not a Lego engineer. But this Lego Star Trek set is a wonderful bit of nostalgia that is also accessible for children.
articles.body: It's not quite a five-year mission, but as Star Trek celebrated its 60th anniversary in September of this year (we may have mentioned it once or twice), I decided it was high time I finally watched the original Star Trek . Before this year, I hadn't seen a single episode of "Star Trek: The Original Series", as it's now known. I'm a millennial; I grew up on "The Next Generation", "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager". By comparison, the old series (TOS) always looked so… old and naff whenever I saw clips of it. But now I have seen the original series. Over the course of 2026, I've ploughed through all 79 episodes, spread across three seasons. And you know what? It's pretty damn good.

articles.title: India's SatLeo Labs wants to build a 'thermometer for Earth' in space
articles.excerpt: The Indian space-tech startup SatLeo Labs is betting that near-real-time temperature data from satellites can help the world stay ahead of escalating climate disasters.
articles.body: AHMEDABAD, India — As climate disasters grow more frequent and severe, a young Indian space-tech startup is betting it can help the world act sooner by reading Earth's temperature from orbit in near-real time. SatLeo Labs, based here in western India, is building what it calls a " thermometer for Earth " in space. It plans to achieve its roadmap to deliver frequent, near-real-time thermal data through Pyro, a planned constellation of 15 microsatellites that will circle the planet in low Earth orbit by early 2030, if all goes to plan.
